info.name: invoice-mgmt API
info.description:
API test suite for the invoice-mgmt Django + DRF backend.

Run the folders IN ORDER - 00 Setup captures the three role tokens and creates the fixtures every later folder depends on, and 99 Teardown removes them and asserts the database is back where it started.

Before the first run, seed the three role accounts:
    cd backend && python manage.py shell < ../postman/seed_test_users.py

Requests named 'KNOWN GAP:' assert the API's CURRENT behaviour at a point where it is wrong or surprising. They are green today. When one goes red, the underlying gap was fixed - update the test, do not revert the fix.

See postman/README.md for the newman command and for the two extract tests that are documented but deliberately not shipped.

item.name: 08 Known gaps
KNOWN GAP: a negative quantity is accepted

request.description: ASSERTS TODAY'S BEHAVIOUR. Neither the model nor the serializer bounds quantity or unit_price, and the migrations carry no CheckConstraint. Note also that frontend lib/money.ts uses Math.round, which gives -0.01 here - the browser preview and the saved total disagree by a cent. If a validator is added, this test goes red: that is the signal to update it.

exec: pm.test("no validator rejects a negative quantity, so the invoice saves", () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.equal(201));
pm.test("the server rounds -0.015 HALF UP (away from zero) to -0.02", () => pm.expect(j.transactions[0].line_total).to.equal("-0.02"));

item.name: KNOWN GAP: due_date before issue_date is accepted

request.description: ASSERTS TODAY'S BEHAVIOUR. Nothing enforces due_date >= issue_date, so such rows inflate the dashboard's overdue_count.

exec: pm.test("a backwards invoice saves cleanly - InvoiceSerializer has no validate()", () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.equal(201));
pm.test("and it then counts as overdue", () => pm.expect(j.due_date < j.issue_date).to.be.true);

item.name: KNOWN GAP: searching by invoice number finds nothing

request.description: ASSERTS TODAY'S BEHAVIOUR. InvoiceList.tsx placeholder reads 'Search invoice number or customer', but search_fields is (customer__name, customer__company_name, notes) and there is no invoice_number filter anywhere. invoice_number is derived from the pk and has no column, so supporting this means parsing the digits back to a pk in the filter layer.

exec: pm.test("the UI advertises this search but the API cannot do it", () => pm.expect(j.count).to.equal(0));
